workLog.task: Make the module's negative assertions survive a rewrap
workLog.outcome: A negative substring check against raw markdown is defeated by a line break inside the banned phrase, and prose is exactly what gets reflowed, so these guards go quietly green on the reintroduction they exist to catch. The review flagged one test. The defect was module-wide: eight sites checked raw text, and the two that already normalized did so as a local convention nobody was obliged to repeat. Rather than add a normalized alias at each site, added _refute(document, *phrases) and routed every markdown negative through it, so the guarantee is one function instead of a habit. The three remaining `not in` assertions are dict-key checks on parsed hooks.json and are unaffected. Table-row positives stay on raw text because their formatting is the assertion.
workLog.evidence: Two independent negative controls, each appending a line-broken copy of a banned phrase to its own source. Reference SKILL.md gained 'The host merges structured\ndecisions from every observer.': the raw assertion passed, _refute failed. Generation SKILL.md gained 'Drops are unsupported\nCopilot events, by design.': same result. Both sources restored; 25 tests pass. ruff check clean. The two ruff format hunks in this file sit at lines 371 and 391, predate the branch, and are #2993 backlog.
